title: proto: wireType 7 on GET /api/v1/nodes — kubelet rejects node object proto encoding
description:
PR #97 CI fails on all kubelet versions with 'proto: illegal wireType 7' when the kubelet tries to read GET /api/v1/nodes/ci-node responses in proto format.

Server logs confirm proto re-encoding IS happening (content_type middleware logs 'proto re-encode kind=Node proto_len=458 json_len=421'), so the response reaches the kubelet as proto bytes. The kubelet then reports wireType 7 when trying to decode it.

wireType 7 is illegal in protobuf3. The most likely cause: a field value in the Node object serializes to a byte that, when treated as a proto tag, has wireType bits = 111 (7). This is a correctness bug in the proto Unknown envelope encoding in crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs or content_type.rs.

Prior fix (PR #84) addressed wireType 6 by skipping proto re-encoding for non-GET requests. This bug is on GET responses, so the skip does not apply.

Diagnostic steps:
1. Decode the proto bytes being sent for a Node object
2. Identify which field produces the wireType 7 byte
3. Fix the encoding in proto.rs

Context: ci-node registers successfully (kubectl get nodes shows it), but the kubelet's own GET to fetch its node object fails to decode.

Blocks: mayor-v43 (pod lifecycle smoke), node reaching Ready in CI.

title: security: no watch concurrency limit per client — unbounded watch stream DoS
description: There is no per-client limit on the number of concurrent watch streams. A single client can open hundreds of watch connections, each pinning a broadcast::Receiver and consuming memory for ring buffer replay events. The InflightLayer caps total concurrency at 50 but a long-lived watch holds its semaphore permit for the full 5-minute max duration, meaning 50 concurrent watches from a single client can exhaust all request slots for all users. Additionally, watch streams hold a broadcast::Receiver that forces the broadcast channel to buffer events for all watchers, amplifying memory pressure.
close_reason: PR #108 opened: per-client watch stream concurrency limit implemented in crates/apiserver/src/

title: security: UID generation uses weak RNG (system time XOR counter), not CSPRNG
description: In handlers/generic.rs, generate_suffix() generates object name suffixes using SystemTime::now().as_nanos() XOR a monotonic counter. This is not a CSPRNG. In handlers/crd.rs, new_uid() formats system time as hex for UIDs. Both are deterministic and predictable. An attacker who knows the server's approximate clock and write count can predict future UIDs, enabling race conditions, pre-image attacks on named resources, or namespace squatting. Kubernetes UIDs must use UUIDv4 from a CSPRNG (rand::OsRng).
close_reason: PR #107 opened: UUIDv4 for generate_suffix() and new_uid() in generic.rs/crd.rs

title: security: no request body size limit — unauthenticated OOM via large body
description: There is no middleware that limits the size of incoming request bodies. An unauthenticated client (or any client with a Bearer token that resolves to a low-privilege user) can POST/PUT a multi-gigabyte body to any writable endpoint. Axum will buffer the full body into memory before auth runs, allowing DoS by OOM. The InflightLayer only limits concurrency (50 total, 20 mutating), not body size. The body size limit must be applied before auth, at the TCP accept or TLS-accept level.
close_reason: PR #107 opened: DefaultBodyLimit::max(4MiB) as outermost layer in main.rs

title: security: static token map uses non-constant-time comparison (timing oracle)
description: In auth.rs, token_map.get(token) uses HashMap lookup which is constant-time for hash buckets but the hash itself is computed from the raw token bytes using a non-cryptographic hasher (SipHash-1-3). An attacker can use timing differences in the hash computation to distinguish a valid token prefix from an invalid one. This is a timing side-channel on authentication.

title: Watch stream audit: verify LIST+WATCH correctness for client-go (resourceVersion, bookmarks, reconnect)
description:
## Goal

Argo CD uses client-go which relies heavily on the watch protocol. Audit the current watch implementation for correctness against what client-go expects.

## What to check

1. **`resourceVersion` on LIST** — client-go does LIST first, then WATCH from the returned `resourceVersion`. Verify LIST response includes `metadata.resourceVersion` at the list level (not just per-item).

2. **WATCH `?resourceVersion=N`** — client-go passes the RV from the LIST. The watch should only send events for changes AFTER that RV. Verify the watch correctly filters by RV.

3. **BOOKMARK events** — client-go sends `?allowWatchBookmarks=true`. The server should periodically emit `{"type":"BOOKMARK","object":{"metadata":{"resourceVersion":"N"}}}` to advance the client's RV without a real event. Check if u7s implements this.

4. **410 Gone handling** — if a client reconnects with a too-old `resourceVersion`, the server should return HTTP 410 with a `StatusReasonExpired` status. Check if u7s returns 410 or silently replays from the beginning.

5. **Initial events (`sendInitialEvents`)** — client-go 0.27+ may send `?sendInitialEvents=true`. Check if u7s handles this correctly (send all current objects as ADDED, then a BOOKMARK, then stream changes).

6. **Chunked encoding** — watch responses must use `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (not Content-Length). Each event is a newline-delimited JSON object.

## Output

Findings doc at `ai/findings/watch-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md` (gitignored). File follow-on beads for each gap found.

## Not blocked by proto fix.

title: Service account token projection: mount SA tokens into pods so in-cluster clients can authenticate
description:
## Goal

Argo CD and any other in-cluster workload authenticates to the API server using a projected SA token mounted at `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token`. Currently u7s defers SA token provisioning (architectural decision DB-05). Without this, no pod can authenticate in-cluster — Argo CD cannot start.

## What's needed

1. **TokenRequest API** (`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/serviceaccounts/{name}/token`) — issues a signed JWT for a given SA, audience, and TTL. The apiserver already has SA signing key infrastructure (`--sa-key`, `--sa-pub`). Use the existing `jsonwebtoken` crate to sign.

2. **Projected volume support in kubelet handshake** — when kubelet creates a pod, it calls TokenRequest to get a token, then mounts it. The apiserver needs to handle this call correctly and return a valid `TokenRequestStatus` with `token` and `expirationTimestamp`.

3. **Token authenticator must accept SA tokens** — the existing token auth currently only handles static CSV tokens. Extend it (or add a new authenticator layer) to validate JWTs signed with the SA key, extract `system:serviceaccount:{ns}:{name}` as the username and `system:serviceaccounts` + `system:serviceaccounts:{ns}` as groups.

## Scope

- `crates/apiserver/src/handlers/` — add `token_request.rs` or add to `pods.rs`/generic
- Route: `POST /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/serviceaccounts/{name}/token`
- `crates/apiserver/src/auth.rs` — extend to validate SA JWTs
- Tests: TokenRequest returns a parseable JWT; JWT authenticates successfully; expired JWT is rejected

## Blocked by

Nothing — independent of proto fix.
close_reason: PR #102 opened: SA token projection correctness fixes (UID in JWT, expiration clamping, default SA seeding)

title: Assign metadata.uid on resource create in generic handler
description:
Pod lifecycle e2e test revealed that metadata.uid is null on all resources created via the generic handler (pods, nodes, all built-in types). Kubelet requires a non-empty UID to name the pod sandbox — without it, cri-o fails with "cannot generate pod name without uid in metadata" and the pod never starts.

Kubernetes assigns a UUID v4 to metadata.uid at create time (server-side). Clients may submit a UID but the server must generate one if absent.

Fix in handlers/generic.rs create_resource / create_namespaced_resource:
- Before writing to the store, if obj["metadata"]["uid"] is null or absent, generate a new UUID v4 and set it
- Use the `uuid` crate (already in Cargo.toml? check) or generate via std if not present
- Same fix needed in handlers/pods.rs create_pod (if pods have a separate create handler)

Also check handlers/cr.rs — stamp_cr_fields already sets uid for CRs, so that path is fine.

Regression test: after create, the returned object must have a non-empty metadata.uid string matching UUID v4 format.

Acceptance: cargo test passes; a pod created via the API has a non-null metadata.uid; kubelet sandbox creation succeeds (end-to-end verifiable).
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix pods/status subresource PATCH so kubelet can report pod phase
description:
Kubelet reports pod lifecycle state by PATCHing PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/status with application/strategic-merge-patch+json. Without this route, pod phase never advances past the initial value and pod lifecycle e2e is impossible.

What's needed:
1. Add PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/status route in handlers/pods.rs
2. Accept application/strategic-merge-patch+json and application/merge-patch+json content types
3. Merge ONLY the .status field of the stored pod with the patch (spec fields must be ignored — kubelet must not be able to overwrite spec via the status subresource)
4. Write back to store and emit a watch event (same as other mutating handlers)
5. Return the updated pod object

Testing policy (Rule 14): extract the status-merge logic into a pure function and test:
- patch with phase=Running on a Pending pod yields Running
- patch that includes a .spec field is ignored (spec field not present in result)
- patch on non-existent pod returns 404
- wrong content-type returns 415

Also check: does GET /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/status already work? If not, add it too (kubelet reads status back after writing).

Acceptance: cargo test passes with ≥4 new unit tests; kubelet no longer logs 404/405 errors on status updates.
close_reason: Closed

title: Extract and test RBAC edge cases: namespace mismatch, resourceNames, ClusterRoleBinding scope
description:

- RoleBinding in namespace "foo" must not grant access in namespace "bar" (namespace mismatch → deny)
- ClusterRoleBinding must still allow when request is namespace-scoped
- Rule with empty resourceNames → matches all names; non-empty resourceNames=["foo"] + request name="bar" → deny
- Mixed pods/pods/log rules: pods/log request vs pods rule must not match

These are silent authorization bypasses — most dangerous class of bug.

Acceptance: 4-5 tests added to rbac.rs that fail if any of the above cases is broken. No handler changes required; rbac.rs logic is already pure-function testable.

title: generic.rs: RBAC index not updated on delete_resource when object has finalizers (soft delete path)
description: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs:678-689, 1044-1053 — The delete_resource and delete_namespaced_resource handlers call apply_delete_policy. When the object has finalizers, the soft-delete path stamps deletionTimestamp and returns early WITHOUT calling rbac_index.remove_object. Later, when the object is hard-deleted via patch (patch_resource, lines 769-780), rbac_index.remove_object IS called. However, between the soft-delete and the hard-delete, the RBAC index still has the entry for a logically-deleted object. For RBAC objects (ClusterRoles, ClusterRoleBindings) this means permissions remain active after the user requests deletion but before finalizers are cleared. This is a security-relevant gap: a soft-deleted ClusterRoleBinding can still grant permissions. Fix: either call rbac_index.remove_object immediately on soft-delete of RBAC objects, or document this as a known limitation and add a test verifying the current (imperfect) behavior.

title: Pod lifecycle smoke test: busybox hello-world via lima-node
description:
Implement and verify a full pod lifecycle smoke test locally using the lima-node VM. The test creates a pod with spec.nodeName=lima-node (bypassing scheduler), waits for it to complete, and checks its logs for 'hello world'. This exercises the full bidirectional kubelet integration: node registration, pod watch delivery, status PATCH, CRI-O image pull and execution, log retrieval. Once the local loop is green, promote to CI as a new workflow job.

Steps:
1. Build u7s-apiserver (cargo build)
2. Start u7s in background with --advertise-address https://host.lima.internal:6443 --ca-key ./ca.key --ca-cert ./ca.crt
3. Wait for kubelet to register the node (kubectl get nodes --watch, timeout 60s)
4. Apply a pod manifest: busybox, command=[sh,-c,echo hello world], restartPolicy=Never, nodeName=lima-node
5. Wait for pod phase=Succeeded (kubectl wait --for=condition=Succeeded, timeout 120s)
6. kubectl logs hello → assert output contains 'hello world'
7. Fix any u7s bugs discovered along the way
8. Once green locally: write as a CI workflow job (probably extend smoke test workflow) and open a PR

The worker should iterate: build → start → test → kill → fix → repeat. Each iteration should be driven by concrete log output from kubelet and u7s.

title: Persist TLS CA key+cert across restarts
description: u7s generates a fresh CA keypair on every startup (tls.rs:generate_tls called unconditionally, KeyPair::generate() always runs). The SA key is already persisted with load-or-generate pattern, but the CA is not. After any restart, the kubeconfig/certs distributed to kubelet (or to the lima VM via lima-start.sh) are signed by the old CA; u7s now trusts a new CA; TLS handshake fails; kubelet falls back to system:anonymous; all requests get 403 Forbidden; node never registers. Fix: apply the same load-or-generate pattern from load_or_generate_sa_keys to the CA key+cert. Persist ca.key and ca.crt alongside sa.key/sa.pub (same --db or key directory). On startup, if the files exist, load them; if not, generate and write. This is the primary blocker for stable lima VM + kubelet integration.

title: Pod watch: implement fieldSelector=spec.nodeName filtering
description:
kubelet watches /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods?watch=true&fieldSelector=spec.nodeName={node} to receive only its own pods. fieldSelector is entirely absent from the codebase (zero occurrences). Without it, the server returns ALL pods in the namespace (Axum drops unknown query params silently), causing kubelet to attempt running unassigned pods.

The watch path is harder: filtering must happen client-side on the stream since the store watch is prefix-based. Emit only events where obj[spec][nodeName] matches.

description: In handlers/crd.rs:create_crd(), there is no validation that the CRD's spec.group does not overlap with built-in API groups (e.g., apps, rbac.authorization.k8s.io, authorization.k8s.io). title: security: no namespace/name path traversal validation on generic handlers

Example: PUT /apis/apps/v1/namespaces/../../secrets/default/target would construct a key that crosses namespace boundaries.

Any authenticated user (or anonymous, if RBAC allows it) can query SubjectAccessReview to probe whether arbitrary users have access to arbitrary resources. In real Kubernetes, SubjectAccessReview requires system:auth-delegator or equivalent permissions. Here, the standard auth middleware gate applies the verb 'create' on 'subjectaccessreviews', but the seed RBAC doesn't restrict it, allowing any user with wide create permissions to probe the RBAC state of other users.

title: security: SA key file written with no explicit permission restriction (world-readable)
description: In tls.rs:load_or_generate_sa_keys(), std::fs::write(sa_key_path, ...) writes the RSA private key to disk using default file permissions (typically 0o644 on Unix). This means the SA signing key is world-readable. Any local process can read the key and mint valid service-account JWTs, gaining cluster-admin equivalent access for any ServiceAccount. The CA key is written the same way. Both keys must be written with 0o600 (owner-only) permissions.

title: security: RBAC index does not prevent privilege escalation via ClusterRoleBinding self-grant

The RBAC engine in rbac.rs applies the binding immediately via apply_object without any escalation check. Kubernetes real RBAC prevents this by requiring the caller to already hold every permission in the referenced role. This is a privilege escalation path: any user who can write ClusterRoleBindings can grant themselves cluster-admin.

title: watch: parse and honour allowWatchBookmarks query parameter
description:
LOW severity conformance gap found in watch audit (mayor-24ig).

CollectionQuery in generic.rs does not include allowWatchBookmarks. The server currently sends periodic BOOKMARK events unconditionally (every 60s and on stream close), regardless of whether the client opted in via ?allowWatchBookmarks=true.

Per the Kubernetes watch protocol, BOOKMARK events should only be sent when the client explicitly requests them. Sending them unconditionally is safe (client-go ignores unexpected bookmarks), but:
1. It wastes bandwidth for clients that did not opt in.
2. It is a conformance deviation that could cause issues with non-client-go consumers.

Fix: add allow_watch_bookmarks: Option<bool> to CollectionQuery; thread the flag through to watch_generic and watch_pods; suppress periodic bookmark emission when the flag is absent or false. The sendInitialEvents BOOKMARK (with k8s.io/initial-events-end annotation) should still be sent unconditionally when sendInitialEvents=true, as that bookmark signals end-of-initial-list rather than a progress marker.

Files: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs (CollectionQuery, watch_generic), crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs (watch_pods)

title: watch: return HTTP 410 before streaming when initial resourceVersion is already expired
description:
MED severity gap found in watch audit (mayor-24ig).

When a client opens a fresh watch with ?resourceVersion=N where N is below the compaction horizon, u7s currently:
1. Returns HTTP 200 OK (flushing headers)
2. Immediately emits a WatchEvent::Compacted as a JSON error body: {"type":"ERROR","object":{"code":410,...}}

This matches kube-apiserver behavior AFTER headers are committed mid-stream. However, for a brand-new watch the Kubernetes API spec says the server SHOULD return HTTP 410 (Gone) directly — before sending any body — so clients can detect the failure synchronously rather than needing to parse the NDJSON error body.

The store's watch() function at lib.rs:696 already yields Compacted immediately if from_revision < horizon. The fix is to check the compaction horizon BEFORE calling state.store.watch() and returning the streaming response. If from_revision > 0 && from_revision < horizon, return a proper HTTP 410 Status response instead of entering the stream.

The mid-stream 410 error body path should remain for cases where compaction happens WHILE watching.

Files: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs (watch_generic or its callers), crates/store/src/lib.rs (expose compaction_horizon check)

title: watch: labelSelector and fieldSelector silently dropped from live watch stream for non-pod resources
description:
HIGH severity gap found in watch audit (mayor-24ig).

In list_resource (generic.rs:510-528) and list_namespaced_resource (generic.rs:958-976), when watch=true the code calls watch_generic() but does NOT pass label_selector or field_selector. These filters are only applied to the initial LIST response.

watch_generic() (generic.rs:219) has no selector parameters at all. Live watch events after the initial list are delivered unfiltered to the client.

By contrast, watch_pods (pods.rs:281) correctly accepts and applies field_selector to live events (pods.rs:378-391).

Impact: client-go watchers using labelSelector or fieldSelector receive ALL events for the resource type. Informer caches may be populated with objects they should not see, causing reconcilers to act on wrong state. For high-volume clusters this also wastes significant CPU/network.

Fix: add label_selector and field_selector parameters to watch_generic(); apply them to each incoming WatchEvent::Added and WatchEvent::Modified before yielding. Deleted events should pass through (client must clean up what it was tracking).

Regression test: watch with labelSelector=app=foo should not receive events for objects with app=bar.

Files: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs (watch_generic, list_resource, list_namespaced_resource)

title: RBAC: enforce api_group on RoleRef and ClusterRoleRef binding resolution
description:
## Goal

Argo CD creates ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings with `roleRef.apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io`. Currently u7s ignores the `api_group` field on RoleRef during RBAC evaluation — it only matches by name. This is a correctness gap that could cause Argo CD's RBAC bindings to match unintended roles if names collide across API groups.

## Current state

`Subject::namespace` and `RoleRef::api_group` are both deserialized but never read (noted in dead code audit). RBAC evaluation in `rbac.rs` does name-only matching.

## Steps

1. In the RBAC evaluator, when resolving a RoleRef, also check that `roleRef.apiGroup` matches the expected group (`rbac.authorization.k8s.io` for ClusterRole/Role, `""` for legacy).
2. Add a test: binding with wrong apiGroup should not grant access.
3. Remove the `#[allow(dead_code)]` on `RoleRef::api_group` once it's wired up (mayor-vm3l covers the annotation removal, but the wiring is the correctness fix here).

title: CRD status subresource: serve /status subresource endpoint for CRs that declare hasStatusSubresource
description:
## Goal

Argo CD writes `.status` on its own CRDs (Application, AppProject) via the status subresource (`PUT /apis/{group}/{version}/{plural}/{name}/status`). Currently u7s serves CRDs without a status subresource — all fields are writable on the main endpoint, which is a conformance gap (noted in architectural memory).

## What's needed

1. When a CRD is created with `spec.versions[].subresources.status: {}`, set `has_status_subresource: true` in the stored `ResourceMeta`.

2. Add route: `PUT /apis/{group}/{version}/{plural}/{name}/status` and `PUT /apis/{group}/{version}/namespaces/{ns}/{plural}/{name}/status` — accepts a full object body but only persists the `.status` field, ignoring spec changes.

3. On the main `PUT`/`PATCH` endpoint for resources with a status subresource, strip `.status` from the incoming body before persisting (status can only be written via the `/status` subresource).

4. `GET /apis/{group}/{version}/{plural}/{name}/status` — returns the full object (same as GET on the main endpoint).

## Tests

- Create a CRD with status subresource; create a CR; PUT to `/status` updates `.status`; PUT to main endpoint does not update `.status`.
- Regression: without status subresource, main PUT persists `.status` normally.

## Not blocked by proto fix.

title: Strategic merge patch (SMP) support for CRs: reject with 415 not 400, or implement basic SMP
description:
## Goal

Argo CD uses strategic merge patch when syncing standard Kubernetes resources. For CRs it typically uses server-side apply or merge patch, but the current rejection message and status code for SMP on CRs needs to be correct.

## Current state

`validate_patch_content_type` in `cr.rs` rejects `application/strategic-merge-patch+json` with HTTP 400. The correct code per the Kubernetes API conventions is **415 Unsupported Media Type**. Argo CD may retry or fail hard depending on the status code.

For built-in resources (Deployments, Services, etc. served through generic.rs), SMP may or may not be implemented — needs checking.

## Steps

1. Change the 400 to 415 in `cr.rs` `validate_patch_content_type` for SMP rejection.
2. Check `generic.rs` patch handler — does it handle `application/strategic-merge-patch+json`? If not, add a 415 rejection with the same pattern.
3. Add regression tests for both.

## Note

Full SMP semantics (list merging by strategic keys) are complex and out of scope here. Correct rejection with 415 is sufficient for now — Argo CD will fall back to merge patch.

## Not blocked by proto fix.

title: CI: auto-update coverage threshold after every merge to main
description:
## Goal

After every merge to main, recompute the coverage threshold and update
`--fail-under-lines N` in `.github/workflows/test.yaml` automatically.
This keeps the gate meaningful without manual intervention.

## Design

Add a new GitHub Actions workflow `.github/workflows/coverage-baseline.yaml`:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
```

Steps:
1. `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --summary-only --json` — parse line coverage %
2. Compute threshold = floor(coverage - 5)
3. Use `sed` to update the `--fail-under-lines N` value in `.github/workflows/test.yaml`
4. If the value changed, commit and push to main with message:
   `ci(coverage): update threshold to N (was M) [skip ci]`
   The `[skip ci]` prevents infinite loop — GitHub Actions skips workflows
   when the commit message contains `[skip ci]`.

## Implementation notes

- Extract coverage % with `jq`: `.data.totals.lines.percent`
- Use `sed -i` to replace `--fail-under-lines [0-9]*` with `--fail-under-lines N`
- Git identity for the commit: use `github-actions[bot]` (standard pattern)
- Only commit if N differs from current value (avoid no-op commits)
- Needs `contents: write` permission on the workflow job

## Quality gates

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`
- Manually verify: push a test commit to main and check the workflow fires
  and updates the value correctly

## Rule 13

Use `jq` + `sed` for JSON extraction and file editing. No Python.

title: CI: enforce per-crate coverage thresholds
description:
## Goal

Establish a coverage gate in `.github/workflows/test.yaml` so CI fails when test coverage drops below a defined threshold. This prevents coverage regressions as the codebase grows.

## Context

PR #89 added a `coverage` job (`cargo llvm-cov --workspace --summary-only`) but with no enforcement — it just measures. Without a threshold, the job is informational only and cannot block regressions.

Industry standard: 80% line coverage is the common gate. Pre-alpha posture: set initial thresholds conservatively (~5% below observed baseline) to avoid flapping gates.

## Steps

1. Check the actual coverage numbers from the first CI run of PR #89 (or run `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --summary-only` locally from main) to establish baselines per crate.

2. Set per-crate thresholds (or a workspace-wide threshold initially):
   - `u7s-store`: target 85%+ (pure logic, easily testable)
   - `u7s-apiserver`: target 65%+ (async handlers covered partly by smoke CI)
   - Workspace overall: use observed baseline minus 5%

3. Update `.github/workflows/test.yaml` `coverage` job to use `--fail-under <N>` (or equivalent llvm-cov flag) so the job exits non-zero when coverage drops below threshold.

4. Commit with a regression test: add a trivial uncovered function to verify the gate fires, then remove it.

5. If `cargo llvm-cov` does not support `--fail-under` directly, use `--json` output + `jq` to extract the totals line and assert `>= N`.

## Quality gates

- `cargo test --workspace`
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --check`
- CI coverage job must exit non-zero on a deliberately-uncovered branch

## Notes

- Do NOT set global threshold before measuring — ground the gate in observed reality
- Per-crate thresholds are better long-term but workspace total is acceptable for initial gate
- Rule 14: gate itself is the regression test

The operator said it does not have to be CoreDNS specifically — any DNS server that works in-cluster is acceptable. Without these, any in-pod API call or DNS lookup fails. Add seed_services() called from main() alongside seed_namespaces() and seed_rbac(). The kubernetes Service needs: name=kubernetes, namespace=default, clusterIP=10.96.0.1, port=443, targetPort=6443. The kube-dns Service needs: name=kube-dns, namespace=kube-system, clusterIP=10.96.0.10, port=53 (UDP+TCP). Both should be idempotent (already-exists is not an error).

title: Add explicit CR status subresource routes and test Gateway API CRD status path
description:
The CR handler (handlers/cr.rs) has no explicit status subresource routes. Status updates for CRs (e.g. Gateway API resources installed as CRDs) currently rely on an implicit fallback in the generic handler (generic.rs lines ~1314-1365), which is untested for the CR case.

Two gaps:
1. No explicit PATCH/PUT/GET routes for /apis/{group}/{version}/{resource}/{name}/status on CRs — confirmed by reading cr.rs (no "status" routes wired)
2. No test confirming that a CR status PATCH actually reaches the store and merges only .status

title: Replace serde_json unwrap() panics with proper 500 error returns in CR/CRD handlers
description:

title: generic.rs: apply_json_patch 'add' to array parent navigates to non-existent intermediate nodes
description: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs:1763-1784 — json_navigate_one returns an error (422) when a path segment is not found in an Object (line 1769-1771). This means a JSON Patch 'add' operation with a path like '/status/conditions/-' will fail with 422 if the 'conditions' key does not exist yet, even though RFC 6902 §4.1 allows 'add' to create intermediate structures. Kubernetes controllers rely on 'add' being able to append to arrays that don't yet exist (e.g., initializing conditions). The current implementation maps 'add' to the same navigation as 'replace', which should only apply to 'replace'. Fix: for 'add' operations, create intermediate objects when a segment is missing; for 'replace', the current strict behavior (422 on missing) is correct. There is no test for add-to-non-existent-array-key in the existing test suite.
close_reason: fixed in PR #73 with regression tests

title: pods.rs: watch stream leaks open on store Compacted even after ERROR event sent
description: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:344-350 — When a WatchEvent::Compacted is received, the handler sends a 410 ERROR event and breaks the loop. However, the Tokio stream from store.watch() is not explicitly cancelled — it is dropped when the async_stream generator ends, which happens after the break. In the current single-generator design this is fine. But last_rv is not updated for Compacted (line 337 does nothing for Compacted), so the 410 response body contains the last-seen revision rather than the compaction horizon. Kubernetes clients use the resourceVersion in the 410 response to decide how far back to relist; sending the wrong revision could cause an infinite relist loop if the client picks a revision still older than the compaction horizon. The WatchEvent::Compacted struct carries both 'requested' and 'horizon' fields — the ERROR response should include the horizon revision. Same issue exists in generic.rs:250-255. Add a test that verifies the 410 ERROR event's resourceVersion matches the compaction horizon.
close_reason: fixed in PR #73 with regression tests

title: state.rs: rbac init key parsing wrong for rolebindings with names containing '/'
description: crates/apiserver/src/state.rs:88 — When populating the RBAC index from store at startup, the namespaced-resource path (roles, rolebindings) uses split_once('/') to split 'rest' into (ns, name). The store key for namespaced resources is /registry/<group>/<plural>/<ns>/<name>. After stripping the prefix, rest = '<ns>/<name>'. split_once('/') correctly handles the normal case. However, if a role name itself contains '/' (which the Kubernetes API forbids for name, but could appear in a corrupted store), split_once gives the wrong name. More critically: the trim_start_matches at line 63 for cluster-scoped resources strips the entire prefix from the key, but if the prefix string appears multiple times in the key (e.g., a name that looks like the prefix), trim_start_matches would strip too much. This is an edge case but could cause RBAC to silently skip entries. The existing test in state.rs only tests that csinodes are registered; there are no tests for rbac init key parsing. Add unit tests for the key-to-api-path conversion logic.
close_reason: fixed in PR #71

title: proto: decode_node_proto uses scan_length_delimited_fields for NodeSpec but NodeSpec has varint fields
description: crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs:269 — decode_node_proto scans NodeSpec (field 2) using scan_length_delimited_fields, which silently skips varint fields (wire type 0) including field 4 (unschedulable: bool). This is silent-skip behavior, not a panic, so it is functionally safe. However, the comment at line 291 says 'unschedulable (varint)' is ignored, and the test at proto.rs:856 only exercises a length-delimited unknown field (field 5, taints). There is no test that verifies the decoder does NOT panic or return None when unschedulable=true (a varint=1) is present in NodeSpec. Real kubelets may send unschedulable nodes. Add a test with a varint NodeSpec.field 4 to confirm the scanner handles it correctly (returns Some, does not panic).

title: tls: partial CA file state causes silent CA rotation on restart
description: crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs:103-151 — load_or_generate_ca checks 'key_exists && cert_exists'. If only one of ca.key / ca.crt exists on disk (e.g., the server crashed between the two fs::write calls at lines 147-149, or ca.crt was manually deleted while ca.key survived), the function regenerates a fresh CA keypair and overwrites ca.key. Any kubelets that already trust the previous CA cert will then see TLS verification failures on the next connection after restart. There is no test for this partial-file scenario and no warning logged. Suggested fix: detect the mismatched state (key_exists XOR cert_exists), log a clear error, and either fail fast or delete the stale file before regenerating. Also add a test that verifies the server errors or recovers correctly when only one CA file is present.
close_reason: fixed in PR #70: XOR partial-state detection, stale file cleanup, tests for both partial-key and partial-cert scenarios

title: Lease renewal: smoke-test kubelet Lease PUT against running server
description:

Concern: replace_namespaced_resource does a conditional put using expected_revision from the incoming body resourceVersion. On first PUT (lease creation), kubelet sends resourceVersion=''. parse_resource_version returns None -> unconditional upsert. On subsequent PUTs kubelet sends the last known resourceVersion. The store behavior for None (unconditional) on a new key must be verified.

Also, create_or_update is false for leases, so POST would fail AlreadyExists on retry, but kubelet uses PUT not POST, so this is fine.

Fix: Write an integration test that: 1) PUTs a Lease with no resourceVersion (should 201/200 create). 2) PUTs again with the returned resourceVersion (should update). 3) PUTs with a stale resourceVersion (should 409 Conflict).

File reference: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs:881-935 (replace_namespaced_resource), crates/apiserver/src/state.rs:175 (lease registry entry).

Severity: MED — lease is the primary kubelet liveness signal; untested path.

title: Node status: add proto decoder for NodeStatus PUT path
description:
PATCH /api/v1/nodes/{name}/status (kubelet heartbeat) is JSON merge-patch and works. PUT /api/v1/nodes/{name}/status goes through core_put_resource_status -> put_resource_status -> extract_body, which calls decode_core_proto_by_kind. The dispatch table in proto.rs:267 only handles Namespace and ConfigMap. If kubelet sends a proto-encoded NodeStatus via PUT, decode_core_proto_by_kind returns None, extract_body falls back to the JSON-start check (raw.first() == Some(&b'{')), which fails for binary proto, returning raw proto bytes. serde_json::from_slice then fails with 'invalid JSON'.

Fix: Add decode_node_proto() to proto.rs mirroring decode_namespace_proto(). Node proto layout: field 1 = ObjectMeta, field 2 = NodeSpec, field 3 = NodeStatus. Add 'Node' => decode_node_proto(raw) to decode_core_proto_by_kind match.

File reference: crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs:266-272 (decode_core_proto_by_kind dispatch table), crates/apiserver/src/util.rs:15-43 (extract_body fallback logic).

Severity: MED — kubelet typically uses PATCH (JSON) for status heartbeats, not PUT with proto, but the code is broken for any PUT path with proto content-type and should be fixed for correctness.
close_reason: PR #55 merged — decode_node_proto() added to proto dispatch table with 3 unit tests. Node PUT path now handles proto-encoded bodies correctly.

This validates resource efficiency under realistic concurrency limits — if handling thousands of requests balloons RSS that is a bug, not a throughput problem. Implement as a new script scripts/bench-rss-load.sh and a new CI job in perf.yaml. The max-inflight limits (50/20) should be enforced by the server via a semaphore or tower middleware layer — the bench also validates that those limits are actually implemented.

title: Conformance: resourceVersion missing from watch ADDED events for initial list replay
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite verifies that watch ADDED events for objects returned in the initial replay (events before the requested resourceVersion) include a populated resourceVersion in metadata. u7s's watch implementation replays events from the ring buffer correctly, but conformance tests assert that each ADDED event's object.metadata.resourceVersion is non-empty and monotonically increasing. If the stored object's resourceVersion is not being propagated into the watch event payload, tests will fail. Verify and fix in store::watch() and encode_watch_event() in generic.rs.

title: Conformance: DELETE response body and finalizer-based soft-delete for all resources
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite verifies that DELETE returns the deleted object (or a Status) in the response body, and that objects with non-empty metadata.finalizers are soft-deleted (deletionTimestamp set, object not removed). u7s currently returns 204 No Content on delete for most resources and does not consistently implement the finalizer soft-delete protocol. Fix needed in delete handlers across namespaces.rs, generic.rs, pods.rs, crd.rs, cr.rs: (1) return the deleted object in the response body (or a Status object), (2) if metadata.finalizers is non-empty, set deletionTimestamp and return the object with 200 instead of deleting.

title: Conformance: Pod status subresource (pods/status) not registered
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite exercises the pods/status subresource: GET/PUT/PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/:ns/pods/:name/status. u7s has status subresource support for generic resources (through generic.rs core_get/put/patch_namespaced_resource_status) and for apps/v1 types, but pods are handled by a dedicated pods.rs handler that does NOT register /status routes. The main.rs router has no route for /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/status. Conformance tests that update pod status (e.g. setting conditions, containerStatuses) via the /status subresource will get 404. Fix: register GET/PUT/PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/status in main.rs, implementing the same pattern as core_get/put/patch_namespaced_resource_status but for the pods store prefix. Note: this is API-level only — it does not require kubelet. Controllers and conformance tests write pod status via the API.

title: Conformance: List pagination (limit/continue tokens)
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite tests list pagination via the limit and continue query parameters. A client can GET /api/v1/pods?limit=10 and receive a response with metadata.continue set to an opaque token; a subsequent GET /api/v1/pods?limit=10&continue=<token> must return the next page. u7s ignores the limit and continue query parameters — it always returns all items. Conformance tests that set limit and check that metadata.continue is populated will fail (they test that the API properly paginates). The store (SqliteStore) would need LIMIT/OFFSET support or a cursor mechanism. The continue token can be a base64-encoded resource version + key offset. Priority note: this is P2 because conformance tests gate on it, but it blocks relatively few tests compared to generateName or fieldSelector.
close_reason: merged in PR #56 (e45a703) — fieldSelector wired to store, limit/continue pagination implemented with base64 cursor tokens, +16 tests

title: Conformance: Namespace deletion must use Terminating phase lifecycle
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite verifies that deleting a namespace transitions it through a Terminating phase before final removal. The expected lifecycle is: DELETE /api/v1/namespaces/:name returns 200 with the namespace in status.phase=Terminating, then the object eventually disappears. u7s currently hard-deletes the namespace immediately on DELETE (delete_namespace in namespaces.rs calls store.delete directly). Conformance tests that watch the namespace and expect a MODIFIED event with phase=Terminating followed by a DELETED event will fail. Fix: on DELETE, stamp status.phase=Terminating and deletionTimestamp, write back, emit MODIFIED watch event. A follow-up GC pass (or immediate second deletion after finalizer check) removes the object. Since u7s has no namespace controller, the simplest correct approach is: if no namespace-level finalizers, still emit the Terminating state then immediately delete.
close_reason: PR #44: Namespace Terminating phase lifecycle before hard-delete

title: Conformance: JSON Patch (application/json-patch+json) support
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite uses JSON Patch (RFC 6902, Content-Type: application/json-patch+json) for some patch operations, particularly on status subresources and in tests that verify atomic field updates. u7s currently only supports application/merge-patch+json and application/strategic-merge-patch+json. A request with application/json-patch+json is rejected with HTTP 415. JSON Patch operations include: add, remove, replace, move, copy, test. Must implement: parse the patch body as an array of RFC 6902 operation objects and apply them to the stored object. The apply logic is independent of the resource type. Recommend using serde_json directly without adding a new crate dependency — the operation set is small enough to implement inline.

title: Conformance: generateName support for object creation
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite creates objects using generateName in metadata instead of a fixed metadata.name. When generateName is set and metadata.name is absent or empty, the API server must generate a unique name by appending a random 5-char alphanumeric suffix to the generateName prefix. u7s currently rejects these requests with 'metadata.name is required' (400) for all resource types — create_pod, create_namespace, create_resource, create_namespaced_resource, create_cr, etc. Conformance tests for Deployments, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and Pods frequently use generateName. Fix: in every create handler, when metadata.name is empty or missing but metadata.generateName is set, generate metadata.name = generateName + random_suffix before storing.

title: Conformance: fieldSelector support for list/watch

Conformance tests that filter by metadata.name will receive more items than expected and fail equality assertions. Must implement at minimum: metadata.name=<value> (exact name filter) and metadata.namespace=<value> filters for list responses. spec.nodeName=<value> for pods would also be needed but requires a field index in the store.

title: feat(apiserver): accept Kubernetes protobuf request bodies
description: kubectl sends write requests (POST/PUT/PATCH) with Content-Type: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf by default. Implementation: detect Content-Type header; if protobuf, decode using the Kubernetes protobuf wire format (k8s.io/apimachinery protobuf encoding — a 4-byte magic prefix followed by proto-encoded Unknown wrapper around JSON or raw proto). The simplest conformance-compatible approach: extract the embedded JSON from the protobuf Unknown envelope rather than implementing full protobuf schema — this handles the common kubectl case without requiring generated proto bindings for every resource type.

title: security audit: MED/LOW cluster — information disclosure, DoS surface, crypto hardening
description:
MED/LOW findings from paranoid security audit (May 2026):

**MED-1: SA JWT audience validation allows only default audience**
File: auth.rs:265-266
The JWT audience is hardcoded to https://kubernetes.default.svc. If a token specifies a different audience (as the TokenRequest API allows via spec.audiences), the auth layer will reject it even though the token is valid. More importantly, there is no mechanism to restrict tokens to specific audiences — all tokens work against all endpoints.

**MED-2: GET /api/v1/{resource} catch-all matches list verb, not get**
File: auth.rs:301 + main.rs:226-229
The method_to_verb mapping maps GET to 'get', but Kubernetes differentiates between 'get' (named resource) and 'list' (collection). A user with 'get' permission on pods but not 'list' can list pods by hitting the collection endpoint because the RBAC check uses verb='get'. This is an authorization bypass for the list verb.

**MED-3: RBAC index not updated atomically on write**
File: rbac.rs:86-117, handlers/generic.rs
When a ClusterRole or ClusterRoleBinding is written via the generic handler, apply_object() is called after the store write succeeds. There is a window between the store write and the RBAC index update where the old policy is still active. Under concurrent writes, this can lead to briefly stale authorization decisions.

**MED-4: expiration_seconds in TokenRequest is uncapped**
File: handlers/tokens.rs:37
A user can set spec.expirationSeconds to u64::MAX (18446744073709551615), creating a token that effectively never expires. Kubernetes limits this to 48 hours. The mint path at line 127 computes exp = now + spec.expiration_seconds, which would overflow on very large values (though u64 arithmetic wraps, the resulting exp would be in the distant past, causing immediate rejection — so this is more a correctness issue than a security one).

**LOW-1: No rate limiting on authentication failures**
An attacker can brute-force static bearer tokens at the speed of network I/O. The inflight limiter (50 concurrent) provides some protection, but token validation is fast (HashMap lookup), so a single connection can try thousands of tokens per second.

**LOW-2: Error messages leak internal key format**
File: store/lib.rs:71, status responses
StoreError::NotFound includes the full internal store key (e.g., /registry/pods/default/nginx). This leaks the internal key structure to clients, which could be useful for constructing path traversal attacks.

**LOW-3: No label/annotation size limits**
Labels and annotations parsed from protobuf or JSON bodies have no size limits. A client can set a single annotation to a multi-megabyte string, consuming disproportionate storage and memory.

**LOW-4: Broadcast channel lag yields approximate compaction horizon**
File: store/lib.rs:721-726
When a watch receiver lags behind the broadcast channel, the Compacted event uses the lag count (n) as the horizon instead of the actual compaction_horizon. This is approximate and could cause clients to relist from the wrong revision.

**LOW-5: HTTP/1.1 only, no HTTP/2**
File: main.rs:548
The server uses hyper::server::conn::http1::Builder, meaning only HTTP/1.1 is served. While not a direct security issue, HTTP/2 multiplexing reduces the number of TCP connections needed and provides better DoS resilience.

**LOW-6: TLS cipher suite selection delegated to rustls defaults**
File: tls.rs:283-285
ServerConfig::builder() uses default cipher suites and protocol versions from rustls. While rustls defaults are generally good (no TLS 1.0/1.1, no weak ciphers), the configuration is not explicitly pinned. A future rustls version could change defaults.

**LOW-7: Kubeconfig written with default file permissions**
File: tls.rs:372
The kubeconfig file (containing client cert and key) is written with default permissions, making it potentially world-readable.
close_reason: PR #119 opened: fix(security): list verb, kubeconfig perms, error message sanitisation

title: Full typed protobuf serialization: generate/write Rust proto bindings for core Kubernetes API types
description:
## Goal

Replace the Unknown-envelope-with-JSON shortcut with proper typed protobuf serialization for core Kubernetes API types. This achieves full wire-format compatibility with client-go's proto path and is required for maximum performance (proto is ~2x smaller and faster to decode than JSON).

## Background

The Kubernetes protobuf format uses per-type generated serializers. Each API type (Namespace, Pod, Node, Service, etc.) has a `.proto` definition in the kubernetes/kubernetes repo under `k8s.io/api/{group}/{version}/generated.proto`. The real kube-apiserver uses code-generated `Marshal()`/`Unmarshal()` for each type.

The Unknown-envelope-with-JSON shortcut (current approach) works for CRDs and is spec-compliant — clients are supposed to check `contentType` in the Unknown envelope. However, some kubectl versions may not honour it, which is the root cause of the current wireType 6 bug (mayor-lsu/mayor-cux).

## Scope

Phase 1 — core/v1 types only (required for kubelet + kubectl compat):
- Namespace, Pod, Node, Service, ConfigMap, Secret, ServiceAccount
- Event, Endpoints
- PersistentVolume, PersistentVolumeClaim (for storage compat)

Phase 2 — extended (for Argo CD + controller compat):
- apps/v1: Deployment, ReplicaSet, StatefulSet, DaemonSet
- rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1: ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding, Role, RoleBinding
- apiextensions.k8s.io/v1: CustomResourceDefinition

## Approach options

**Option A** — Use `prost` crate with Kubernetes proto files:
- Copy `.proto` files from kubernetes/kubernetes into the repo
- Use `prost-build` to generate Rust structs
- Write conversion functions `serde_json::Value → proto struct → bytes`
- Pro: auto-generated, low maintenance. Con: conversion layer is non-trivial, proto files are large.

**Option B** — Hand-write proto serializers for each type:
- Similar to the current `encode_proto_response` but per-type
- Pro: full control, no build deps. Con: ~500 LoC per type × 15 types = significant.

**Option C** — Extend the Unknown envelope shortcut correctly:
- Keep Unknown envelope but ensure contentType is respected by testing against the exact client-go version used in CI
- If client-go truly ignores contentType, file a bug upstream
- Pro: 10x less work. Con: may not achieve full compat.

## Recommendation

Option A (prost) if Option C proves insufficient. Do not start until mayor-oayj (serializer abstraction) is merged and the current wireType 6 bug is resolved — that resolution will clarify whether Option C is viable.

## Blocked by

- mayor-oayj (serializer abstraction — prerequisite)
- Resolution of mayor-lsu (wireType 6 bug — determines if Option C is viable)

## Important finding (2026-05-21)

client-go's RawSerializer (used for write response decoding) bypasses the contentType field in the Unknown envelope entirely. It always tries to decode field 2 (raw) as a typed proto message. The Unknown+JSON shortcut is therefore NOT viable for write responses.

For GET responses (kubelet reads), the contentType path may still work — kubelet uses a different decode path. Monitor kubelet smoke tests after PR #84 merges to confirm GET proto still works.

If GET proto also needs to be real typed proto, mayor-pgdr becomes P1.

title: Remove #[allow(dead_code)] suppressions: delete dead items, drop stale annotations
description:
## Audit findings (2026-05-21)

9 suppressions found. 4 to eliminate, 5 to keep with comments.

### Actions

**DELETE these items entirely (3):**

1. `crates/apiserver/src/types.rs` — `Object::namespace()` — zero callers anywhere; namespace read directly from JSON at all call sites
2. `crates/apiserver/src/types.rs` — `Object::resource_version_u64()` — zero callers; resource version manipulated as string or via `set_resource_version(u64)`
3. `crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs` — `test_temp_dir()` inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` — uncalled test helper

**DELETE the annotation only (1), code is fine:**

4. `crates/apiserver/src/auth.rs:40` — `UserInfo::uid` — field IS read in production at `handlers/authorization.rs:279`; the `#[allow(dead_code)]` is stale from before TokenReview was wired up

**KEEP+COMMENT (5, no code change needed):**

- `mcp-server/src/main.rs:14` — `U7sTools::tool_router` — consumed by `#[tool_router]` proc macro via `ServerHandler`; rustc can't see macro-generated usage
- `types.rs:166` — `ResourceMeta::namespaced` — only read in `#[cfg(test)]` assertion blocks
- `auth.rs:56` — `SaClaims::iss` — deserialized for schema completeness; issuer validated by jsonwebtoken before the field is read
- `rbac.rs:23` — `Subject::namespace` — deserialized for schema compliance; RBAC name-only matching for now; comment already present
- `rbac.rs:31` — `RoleRef::api_group` — same pattern; comment already present

## Quality gates

- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` must pass after deletions
- `cargo test --workspace` must pass (no test regressions from deleting dead items)
- `cargo fmt --check`

## Rule 14

Delete tests are inherent (removing dead code can't break existing callers — if it does, the callers would surface as compile errors). The stale annotation removal (UserInfo::uid) is verified by clippy passing clean.

title: Add unit tests for patch.rs strategic-merge edge cases: multiple deletes, empty merge key, replace directive
description:
patch.rs strategic_merge_array (lines 115-193) has 4 tests covering the happy path and basic directives. Missing coverage for edge cases that could silently corrupt data:

- Multiple \$patch:delete directives in same patch — must delete all matching elements
- \$patch:replace directive — replaces entire array; subsequent patches must not apply
- Merge on element with no merge key — should append or return an error (not silently drop)
- Empty string merge key in \$patch:delete element — must error cleanly, not panic

Acceptance: 4 tests added to patch.rs that each fail if the edge case is mishandled. No implementation changes unless a bug is actually found (file separately if so).

description: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:120-172 — The store FieldSelector extraction (splitting on '=', skipping '!=') is copy-pasted identically at lines 120-130 (watch path) and 157-168 (list path). This is the same pattern extracted into parse_field_selector() in generic.rs:338. The duplication means any bug fix or extension (e.g., supporting != at the store layer) must be applied in three places. Fix: extract the pod-specific field-selector-to-store conversion into a small helper function, or reuse parse_field_selector from generic.rs if pods are moved to that path.

title: Node proto decoder: preserve NodeSpec and NodeStatus fields
description: decode_node_proto in proto.rs (lines 244-271) extracts only ObjectMeta from the protobuf. NodeSpec (field 2) and NodeStatus (field 3) are silently discarded. When kubelet POSTs a new Node via protobuf (the default Content-Type), the stored Node has empty spec and no status. Kubelet then PATCHes /api/v1/nodes/<name>/status which restores status fields, but NodeSpec (podCIDR, providerID, taints) remains permanently empty. This causes the node to appear malformed to controllers and may trigger retry loops in kubelet. Fix: extend decode_node_proto to capture spec and status fields, or convert the incoming protobuf to JSON and merge with existing stored object. Medium complexity.

title: UID generation calls SystemTime::now() twice — cosmetic race
description: new_uid() in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/crd.rs:123 and new_cr_uid() in cr.rs:119 each call SystemTime::now() twice (once for secs, once for nanos), reading from two separate instants. title: Build custom MCP server using modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk for structured diagnostics and bd integration
description:
The modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk) is the official Anthropic-maintained Rust SDK for building MCP servers. This is what we should use to build a custom MCP server for u7s tooling — NOT mcp-language-server (abandonware).

What to build: a small MCP server binary (crates/mcp-server or similar) that:
1. Wraps cargo check/clippy output as structured MCP tool calls (get_diagnostics -> [{file, line, col, severity, message}])
2. Wraps bd commands (list, show, ready) as MCP tools so agents can query beads without shell
3. Potentially wraps git status/diff as structured tools

Use the official Rust SDK: cargo add modelcontextprotocol-sdk (check crates.io name). Build as a standalone binary. Wire into .mcp.json at project root.

Why: workers currently parse cargo/clippy stdout. Structured diagnostics reduce hallucinated line numbers and enable faster fix loops.

title: Add max watch duration — stuck clients hold streams forever
description: handlers/pods.rs:166-251 watch_pods stream has no timeout or max-duration enforcement. The Kubernetes spec requires servers to terminate watch streams after a server-defined max duration (typically 5-10 minutes) and send a BOOKMARK before closing. A stuck or abandoned client currently holds the stream open indefinitely. Fix: add a max watch duration (configurable, default 5 minutes) using tokio::time::sleep or interval. On expiry, emit a final BOOKMARK with the last_rv and close the stream gracefully. Apply the same pattern when generic watch is implemented (mayor-4z5).

Optionally remove the unused prefix field from InternalEvent entirely.
